uncertainties: (1) Financial Impact Estimating Conference: the task note names it, but no FIEC statement exists for this legislatively referred measure; the official fiscal source is the Revenue Estimating Conference revenue-impact analysis (REC page numbers 682-699). The DOS page's financial-impact fields are blank. (2) Fiscal-year vs tax-year labels: TF says 'as of tax year 2031', REC prints cash by fiscal year 2030-31 (-$10,710.2M) and treats the recurring -$11,834.7M as the 6th-year (FY2031-32) cash impact; Walczak says 'FY 2032'. Use the REC wording, or say 'recurring' and 'by 2031-32'. (3) TF's phrase 'the $150,000 exemption would cost $4.9 billion' mis-scopes the REC figure, which includes the 5% non-homestead cap. (4) The ~15% rental incidence is Walczak's modelled upper-bound scenario assuming full revenue-neutral millage backfill; TF reports it without the caveat; Walczak also gives 96.1% recoverability under the 10-mill caps; actual local responses are unknown and the REC explicitly scores local responses as zero. (5) Walczak's study is funded/supported by rental-industry and housing-advocacy partners and is not peer reviewed. (6) Newcomer wait: 'five years' (TF), 'fifth year of exemption' (AG text, DOS), 'four years' at the lower amount (REC) - choose the AG/ballot wording. (7) TF's cited Rolheiser paper and several Census/DOR tables were not independently fetched; TF's own table figures (millage tables) rest on Florida DOR data TF cites. (8) The circuit court order was not retrieved; the quoted phrases come from WFLX/Local10/AP reporting of the order; the AG letter PDF has no text layer so ag_letter_transcription.txt is a T0 hand transcription (confirm against ag_page-1.png/ag_page-2.png). (9) Whether anyone challenged the revised statement within the 10-day window or sought Supreme Court review was not established beyond Florida Politics' statement that the state did not appeal; a docket search is needed before the post-vote page asserts there was no further litigation. (10) Lincoln explainer vs primary: the existing wiki sentence 'direct the legislature toward exempting homesteads entirely' and 'raise ... to $250,000 by 2028' should be tightened against the enrolled text ($150,000 in 2027; Legislature must prescribe a procedure for local governments to opt up to full exemption). (11) Post-vote: the Division of Elections results (3 Nov 2026) and the 60% threshold outcome are unknown; the paragraph should be dated and the page updated or superseded after the vote.
